rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent that does not resolve strands the reader mid-slide. Closest candidates checked: chunk 1 (3-9) line 5 'In one, the first prompt is' and line 7 'In the other session' both resolve against 'Two Claude Code sessions' named at line 3, same chunk; line 7 'Take a guess before it runs' resolves 'it' against 'the same second prompt: dinner' two clauses earlier, same chunk; line 9 'The first exchange became part of context' resolves against 'the first prompt' named twice in the same chunk. Chunk 2 (11-15) line 13 'Context is whatever you tell it' — 'it' = Claude, a proper noun introduced by name four times in chunk 1 (lines 5, 5, 7, 7) and reused here, which is the compendium's explicit NOT-a-violation case (term introduced on an earlier slide, reused). Line 15 'The move is loading the right context before the question' reads as the chunk's own header ('You steer the answer by loading context') restated in the same chunk, not a dangling forward or backward pointer. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent anywhere in the current 2-chunk body. PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reveal narrated before its guess kills the live demo's payoff. Chunk 1 (3-9): guess instruction at line 7 ('Take a guess before it runs. What does Claude suggest now?') precedes the reveal at line 9 ('Something Finnish: salmon, rye bread, meatballs.') — guess before outcome, same chunk, correct order. Matches the maintainer block's own accept-note (L21: 'Guess before reveal. The guess paragraph precedes the Finnish-dinner answer.'). PASS.

Harm: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet projects as a slide that says nothing standalone. Chunk 1 (3-9) carries the full demo plus reveal; chunk 2 (11-15) carries the steering claim plus its restatement. Both self-carry. Chunk 0 is the title-only opener (no lede, per the maintainer block's own standing constraint 'Openers carry no setup lede') — that is the template's defined title-slide shape, not the wait-state/context-dependent-bullet failure this rule targets. PASS, no orphan.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a reader skimming only headers. 'Context is King' (chunk 1) is delivered exactly: the same second question gets two different answers depending on what came before. 'You steer the answer by loading context' (chunk 2) is restated near-verbatim at line 15 ('The move is loading the right context before the question'). Both headers are true summaries of their chunk's content. PASS.

Harm: a cadence tic reads as authorial clutter under slide density. Checked all six sub-patterns across chunks 0-2 (lines 1-15): (1) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple — grep -inE 'Not [A-Za-z][^.]*\. *Not [A-Za-z]' on the body view → 0 hits (the pre-existing 'Not by reading about it.' line lived only in the now-removed 'The loop is what you repeat' section per the d065f8bc..HEAD diff and is absent from the current body). (2) anaphora/epistrophe triples — none. (3) self-grading superlatives — grep -inE 'one of the (most|best)' → 0 hits. (4) number + own retraction — body prose contains zero digits (grep -noE '[0-9]+' against the body view matches nothing). (5) abstraction-noun stacks — body stays concrete throughout (capital of Italy, pasta/osso buco/risotto, largest lake in Finland, salmon/rye bread/meatballs). (6) verb triplets with an empty leg — none. PASS on all sub-items; no self-grading-superlative hit, so this row carries no value-prop-leak blocking instance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a label-shaped header on a lecture wastes the beat where a law should be named. This file is a lecture, so headings owe claims: 'Context is King' (a maxim/claim) and 'You steer the answer by loading context' (a claim about reader agency) — both claims, neither a bare label or phase tag. This rule postdates the template's explicit blocking/non-blocking partition (added after the rules-9-14 gap noted in the template); applying the stated principle ("I cannot follow this" = blocking, "this could be tighter" = TODO), a label-shaped header would cost the reveal-a-law beat, not comprehension — classified non-blocking, consistent with header-adjacent rule 6. PASS, no violation either way.
